Summary: Curriculum Definition & Identity Management
Description: Create and maintain the authoritative curriculum aggregate linked to an ACD-01 course, with tenant/campus/department scoping. Satisfies FR-01, BR-05, BR-13.

Summary: Create a new draft curriculum
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create a new curriculum aggregate linked to an active ACD-01 course, so that a governed draft curriculum exists for a given academic period before versions are built out.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am an authenticated Academic Admin with CURRICULUM_CREATE permission, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula with courseId, academicPattern, academicYear, departmentId, campusId and name, Then a new curricula document is persisted with status=DRAFT and a first curriculum_versions document at version=1, And a CurriculumCreated event is written to the outbox, And the response returns curriculumId, version and status per the Standard Response envelope (FR-01, UC-01).

Summary: Validate courseId resolves through ACD-01
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to validate that courseId resolves to an active course in ACD-01 before creating or updating a curriculum, so that no curriculum can exist for an invalid or inactive course.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a courseId is supplied on create, When the service validates it against ACD-01's course reference API, Then the request succeeds only if the course exists and is active, otherwise ACD2_COURSE_INVALID (422) is returned and no document is written (BR-05, Exceptions §15).

Summary: Enforce tenant/campus/department scope consistency
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to enforce that a curriculum's tenantId/institutionId/campusId scope matches the referenced course and any mapped subjects, so that curricula never span mismatched tenant boundaries.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum references a course or subject from a different tenant/campus scope, When the request is validated, Then it is rejected with a 403/422 tenant-mismatch error, consistent with BR-13 and the Exceptions table's 'Tenant mismatch' scenario.

Summary: View curriculum detail
Description: As an authorized user (Faculty, Committee, Registrar, Management), I want to retrieve the full detail of a specific curriculum, so that I can review its current authoritative definition and effective version.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a valid curriculumId and a user with CURRICULUM_VIEW permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id} is called, Then the current curriculum document (with its effective version reference) is returned with HTTP 200 (UC-11).

Summary: Enforce read-only access for the Student Portal
Description: As a Student, I want to view only published, active curriculum information through the Student Portal, so that I can understand my programme structure without seeing draft or internal-only detail.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Student, When I access curriculum data via the Student Portal, Then only PUBLISHED/effective curriculum content is returned and it is strictly read-only, consistent with the Student Portal (Read Only) channel shown in the architecture diagram.

Summary: Curriculum Catalog & Search
Description: Provide indexed, filterable, paginated search/list across curricula and a list of currently active curricula. Satisfies FR-14 and the /active and /search endpoints.

Summary: Search and filter curricula
Description: As an authorized user, I want to search and filter curricula by course, department, academic year and status with pagination, so that I can quickly find the curriculum I need in a large catalog.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/academics/curricula with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then results are returned within the P95 <500 ms indexed-read target, and only fields appropriate to my role/classification are included (FR-14, NFR §16).

Summary: List active curricula
Description: As Faculty, Student or Management, I want to list all currently active/effective curricula, so that I can see what is live for the institution right now without filtering through drafts and history.
Acceptance Criteria: Given one or more curricula have a PUBLISHED/EFFECTIVE version, When I call GET /api/v1/active (or the equivalent filtered list endpoint), Then only curricula with an effective version are returned (API Design panel, diagram endpoint list).

Summary: Curriculum Version Management
Description: Create, update, publish and retrieve immutable curriculum versions so exactly one version is ever effective per course/academic period, and history is always reconstructable. Satisfies FR-02, FR-03, FR-09, FR-10, BR-01, BR-02, BR-11, BR-12.

Summary: Create a new curriculum version for an academic period
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create a new draft version of a curriculum for a given academic period, so that curriculum content can be built up and revised before publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum exists, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions with effectiveFrom/effectiveTo and regulation details, Then a new curriculum_versions document is created in DRAFT status, and a CurriculumVersionCreated event is emitted (FR-02, UC-02, Sequence Diagram panel 6).

Summary: Update a draft curriculum version
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to update the fields of a curriculum version while it is still DRAFT, so that I can refine its structure before submission for approval.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum_versions document is in status=DRAFT, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v} with changed fields, Then the draft is updated in place, And attempting the same update once the version is PUBLISHED is rejected with ACD2_VERSION_IMMUTABLE (409) (FR-03, BR-02, Exceptions §15).

Summary: Enforce exactly one effective version per course/academic period
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to guarantee that only one curriculum version may be effective for a given course and academic period, so that there is never ambiguity about which curriculum applies.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course/academic-period pair already has an effective published version, When another version for the same course/academic period is published, Then the prior version is atomically superseded within the same transaction, and any attempt to publish an overlapping effective period without superseding is rejected with a 409 conflict (BR-01, Exceptions §15 'Overlapping effective periods').

Summary: Prevent mutation of published versions
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to reject any attempt to modify a published curriculum_versions document, so that historical reconstruction always remains trustworthy.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum_versions document has status=PUBLISHED, When any update operation targets that document directly, Then the operation is rejected with ACD2_VERSION_IMMUTABLE (409) and no field is altered (BR-02, BR-12).

Summary: Retrieve version history for a curriculum
Description: As an authorized user, I want to list all versions of a curriculum, so that I can review how it has evolved across academic periods.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculumId with one or more versions, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions, Then all versions are returned ordered by version number with status and effective dates.

Summary: Retrieve a specific historical curriculum version
Description: As an authorized user, I want to fetch a specific past version of a curriculum, so that I can reconstruct exactly what was in effect during a prior academic period.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculumId and a version number that exists, When I call GET /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}, Then the immutable snapshot for that version is returned unchanged from when it was published (BR-12).

Summary: Clone the effective version into a new draft for annual revision
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to clone the current effective curriculum version into a new draft, so that I can perform an annual revision without re-entering the entire structure from scratch.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum has a currently effective version, When I initiate an annual revision, Then a new draft version is created pre-populated with the effective version's semesters, subjects, syllabus, credits and outcomes, ready for edits, per Workflow 14.2 (Annual Revision).

Summary: Reject stale writes with optimistic version locking
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to detect when a client submits an update based on a stale version, so that two concurrent edits cannot silently overwrite each other.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a client submits an update based on a stale version reference, When the write is attempted, Then it is rejected with ACD2_VERSION_CONFLICT (409) instructing the client to reload the latest version (Exceptions §15 'Stale version').

Summary: Semester & Subject Mapping
Description: Define semester structure within a curriculum version and map active ACD-03 subjects to semesters, with uniqueness and duplicate-mapping controls. Satisfies FR-04, BR-06, BR-07, BR-08.

Summary: Add a semester to a curriculum version
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a semester (sequence number, name, academic year) to a curriculum version, so that subjects can subsequently be mapped into a defined structure.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=DRAFT, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/semesters with semesterNo, name and academicYear, Then a semester entry is added to the version (UC-03, Domain Model panel 5).

Summary: Enforce unique semester sequence numbers within a version
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to enforce that semesterNo is unique within a curriculum version, so that the academic structure is never ambiguous.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a semesterNo already exists within the target curriculum version, When another semester is added with the same number, Then the request is rejected with a validation error (BR-07).

Summary: Map a subject to a semester
Description: As an Academic Admin or Faculty, I want to map an active ACD-03 subject to a semester with its order, type, credits, contact hours and mandatory flag, so that the curriculum's subject structure is fully defined.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a semester exists in the curriculum version, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/subjects with subjectId, semesterNo, subjectOrder, subjectType, credits, contactHours and mandatory, Then the subject reference is validated against ACD-03, a curriculum_subjects mapping is persisted, and a CurriculumSubjectMapped event is emitted (FR-04, BR-06, UC-04, sample Map Subject Request §29.2).

Summary: Validate subjectId resolves through ACD-03
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to validate that subjectId resolves to an active, non-deprecated subject in ACD-03 before mapping, so that curricula can never reference an inactive or nonexistent subject.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subjectId is supplied on a mapping request, When the service validates it against ACD-03's subject reference API, Then the request succeeds only if the subject is active, otherwise ACD2_SUBJECT_INVALID (422) is returned and no mapping is persisted (BR-03, BR-06).

Summary: Prevent duplicate subject-to-semester mapping
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to reject mapping the same subject to the same semester more than once, unless an explicit repeat/elective policy permits it, so that curriculum structure stays unambiguous.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a subject is already mapped to a semester in the target version, When a duplicate mapping is submitted without an applicable repeat/elective policy exception, Then the request is rejected with ACD2_DUPLICATE_MAPPING (409) (BR-08).

Summary: Remove a subject-to-semester mapping
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to remove an existing subject mapping from a draft version, so that I can correct the curriculum structure before publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a mapping exists in a DRAFT version, When I call DELETE /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/subjects/{mappingId}, Then the mapping is removed and a CurriculumSubjectUnmapped event is emitted (API Design §28, Event Contracts §31).

Summary: Flag mappings when a referenced subject is deactivated
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to consume SubjectDeactivated events from ACD-03 and flag affected curriculum_subjects mappings, so that publication is blocked for curricula referencing a now-inactive subject.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a SubjectDeactivated event is received for a subjectId referenced by one or more mappings, When the event is processed, Then affected mappings are flagged and any pending publication referencing them is blocked, consistent with 'Flag affected mappings; block publication if invalid' (Event Consumption §32).

Summary: Syllabus & Credit Management
Description: Maintain module/topic-level syllabus structure and credit allocation per curriculum version, validated against configured academic credit policy. Satisfies FR-05, BR-09.

Summary: Define syllabus structure for a curriculum version
Description: As Faculty or an Academic Admin, I want to define the module/topic-level syllabus structure for a curriculum version, so that the approved curriculum carries a complete, structured syllabus.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=DRAFT, When I PUT /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/syllabus with the module/topic structure, Then the syllabus structure is persisted against the version and a CurriculumSyllabusUpdated event is emitted (FR-05, UC-05, Event Contracts §31).

Summary: Retrieve syllabus structure for a version
Description: As Faculty, Student or EXM, I want to retrieve the syllabus structure for a specific curriculum version, so that I can review or consume the approved teaching structure.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version has a defined syllabus, When GET /api/v1/curricula/{id}/syllabus is called, Then the current syllabus structure for that version is returned (API Design panel, diagram endpoint list).

Summary: Validate credit totals against configured academic policy
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to validate that a curriculum version's total credits satisfy the institution's configured academic credit policy, so that no curriculum can be published with an invalid credit structure.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version's aggregated subject credits are computed, When a submit-for-approval or publish action is attempted and the total violates configured policy (min/max), Then the action is rejected with ACD2_CREDIT_POLICY (422) detailing the violation (BR-09, Exceptions §15 'Credit policy violation').

Summary: Learning Outcome Mapping
Description: Maintain curriculum-level learning outcome (CO/PO) references so curriculum elements are traceable to outcomes for accreditation and effectiveness reporting. Satisfies FR-06.

Summary: Add a learning outcome reference to a curriculum version
Description: As Faculty or an Academic Admin, I want to add a learning outcome (CO/PO) reference to a curriculum version, so that curriculum elements are traceable to defined learning outcomes for accreditation reporting.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version exists, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/outcomes with code, description, bloomLevel and type (CO/PO), Then a curriculum_outcomes document is persisted and a CurriculumOutcomeUpdated event is emitted (FR-06, Domain Model panel 5, Event Contracts §31).

Summary: List learning outcomes for a curriculum version
Description: As Faculty, Accreditation Team or Management, I want to list all learning outcomes mapped to a curriculum version, so that I can verify outcome coverage for accreditation review.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version has mapped outcomes, When GET /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/versions/{v}/outcomes is called, Then all outcome references for that version are returned (API Design §28).

Summary: Curriculum Prerequisite Management
Description: Maintain curriculum-level prerequisite relationships with cycle prevention. Satisfies FR-07, BR-10.

Summary: Add a curriculum prerequisite
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a prerequisite relationship at the curriculum level, so that structural academic dependencies between curricula are governed and enforceable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given both curricula referenced in the relationship exist and are valid, When I POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/prerequisites, Then the relationship is validated for cycles and persisted, and a CurriculumPrerequisiteUpdated event is emitted (FR-07, Event Contracts §31).

Summary: Reject curriculum prerequisite cycles
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to detect and reject any prerequisite relationship that would create a cycle in the curriculum prerequisite graph, so that eligibility logic downstream never enters an unresolvable loop.
Acceptance Criteria: Given adding a proposed prerequisite edge would create a cycle, When the add-prerequisite request is validated, Then it is rejected with ACD2_PREREQUISITE_CYCLE (422) and no edge is persisted (BR-10, Exceptions §15).

Summary: List prerequisites for a curriculum
Description: As an authorized user, I want to view the full set of active prerequisites for a curriculum, so that I understand its dependency chain before approval or publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculumId, When I query its prerequisites, Then all active prerequisite relationships are returned via an indexed lookup.

Summary: Approval & Publication Workflow
Description: Route draft curriculum versions through a governed submit → review → approve → publish workflow before they become effective. Satisfies FR-08, FR-09, BR-04, BR-14, UC-06 through UC-09.

Summary: Submit a draft curriculum version for approval
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to submit a draft curriculum version for approval, so that it enters the governed review workflow before publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=DRAFT and passes structural validation, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/submit, Then the status transitions to REVIEW, a CurriculumSubmitted event is emitted, and the approval workflow is initiated (FR-08, UC-06, Curriculum Lifecycle §13).

Summary: Department Head or Curriculum Committee reviews a submitted curriculum
Description: As a Department Head or Curriculum Committee member, I want to review a submitted curriculum version, so that only academically vetted curricula proceed toward approval.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=REVIEW and belongs to my department/committee scope, When I record my review decision, Then the decision is captured and, on rejection, the version returns to DRAFT/REVISION per the lifecycle diagram (UC-07, Curriculum Lifecycle §13).

Summary: Approve a reviewed curriculum version
Description: As a Registrar or authorized approver, I want to approve a curriculum version that has passed review, so that it becomes eligible for publication.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version has completed review, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/approve, Then the status transitions to APPROVED and a CurriculumApproved event is emitted (UC-08, RBAC §48).

Summary: Publish an approved curriculum version
Description: As a Registrar, I want to publish an approved curriculum version, so that it becomes the institution's single effective curriculum for that course/academic period.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version is in status=APPROVED and all publication invariants (BR-14) are satisfied, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/publish, Then the version becomes effective, any prior effective version is superseded, and a CurriculumPublished event is emitted to ACD-01/03, EXM, LMS and Analytics (FR-09, UC-09, Workflow §14.1).

Summary: Block publication until approval and structural validation are complete
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to block publication until approval is recorded and every structural/reference validation passes, so that no incomplete or unapproved curriculum ever becomes effective.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version lacks approval or fails any mandatory validation (invalid subject, credit policy, duplicate mapping, prerequisite cycle), When a publish action is attempted, Then it is blocked with ACD2_PUBLICATION_BLOCKED (409) identifying the failing condition, and no partial publish state is possible (BR-04, BR-14, Exceptions §15 'Approval missing').

Summary: Curriculum Lifecycle & Retirement
Description: Supersede and retire historical curriculum versions without deleting evidence, and prevent deletion where academic downstream references exist. Satisfies FR-10, BR-15, UC-10.

Summary: Retire a curriculum or version
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to retire a curriculum or a specific historical version, so that it is marked no longer applicable while its history remains fully intact.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version is SUPERSEDED or otherwise eligible for retirement, When I call POST /api/v1/academics/curricula/{id}/retire, Then the status transitions to RETIRED, a CurriculumRetired event is emitted, and no data is deleted (FR-10, UC-10, Curriculum Lifecycle §13).

Summary: Prevent deletion of curricula with downstream academic references
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to reject deletion of a curriculum that has downstream academic references (exam schemes, LMS content, enrollment history), so that referential integrity across the platform is never broken.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum has one or more downstream academic references, When a delete request is attempted instead of retirement, Then the request is rejected, consistent with BR-15's 'retirement is used instead' rule.

Summary: Automatically supersede the prior version on publish
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want the previously effective version to be automatically marked SUPERSEDED within the same transaction as a new publish, so that exactly one version is ever effective and the transition is atomic.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum has a currently effective version, When a new version is published, Then the prior version's status is atomically updated to SUPERSEDED in the same MongoDB transaction as the publish (Workflow §14.2, Transaction Strategy §56).

Summary: Event-Driven Integration
Description: Reliably publish the full curriculum domain event catalog via a transactional outbox and consume upstream ACD-01/ACD-03 reference-data events, so ACD-01/03, EXM, LMS and Analytics stay eventually consistent. Satisfies FR-11.

Summary: Publish domain events via transactional outbox
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want every state-changing operation to write its domain event (CurriculumCreated, CurriculumVersionCreated, CurriculumSubmitted, CurriculumApproved, CurriculumPublished, CurriculumRetired, CurriculumSubjectMapped, CurriculumSubjectUnmapped, CurriculumSyllabusUpdated, CurriculumOutcomeUpdated, CurriculumPrerequisiteUpdated) to a transactional outbox in the same transaction as the business write, so events are never lost even if the broker is temporarily unavailable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum create/version/mapping/workflow operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event from the Event Contracts catalog (§31) is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged (Event Architecture §30).

Summary: Emit CurriculumPublished to all downstream consumers
Description: As a downstream service (ACD-01, ACD-03, EXM, LMS, Analytics), I want to receive a CurriculumPublished event with the effective curriculum data, so that I can update my local projection without querying ACD-02 directly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version is published, When the CurriculumPublished event is emitted, Then it includes eventId, entityId, tenantId, version and the effective curriculum data per the Representative Event schema (§31.1), and all listed consumers can deserialize and apply it.

Summary: Consume CourseDeactivated/CourseArchived and flag affected curricula
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to consume CourseDeactivated and CourseArchived events from ACD-01, so that curricula referencing a now-inactive or archived course are flagged and blocked from new publication without deleting their history.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a CourseDeactivated or CourseArchived event is received for a courseId referenced by one or more curricula, When the event is processed, Then affected curricula are flagged, new publication is prevented, and their historical records are preserved unchanged (Event Consumption §32).

Summary: Deduplicate inbound events using eventId
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want to deduplicate inbound events by eventId, so that redelivered or replayed events never cause duplicate side effects.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound event with an eventId already processed successfully, When it is redelivered, Then the service recognizes the duplicate and skips reprocessing without error (Event Consumption §32).

Summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want events that repeatedly fail processing to be routed to a dead-letter queue after retries are exhausted, so that they can be investigated and replayed without blocking the main stream.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound or outbound event fails processing after the maximum configured retry attempts, When retries are exhausted, Then the event is persisted to dead_letter_events with failure context and an alert is raised (Retry Strategy §54, Monitoring §52).

Summary: Idempotency, Concurrency & Transaction Integrity
Description: Guarantee safe client retries on create-version/mapping/lifecycle commands and correct concurrent-edit handling across curriculum, version, and history writes. Satisfies §54, §55, §56.

Summary: Support idempotent create-version, mapping and lifecycle requests
Description: As an API client, I want to supply an idempotency key on create-version, subject-mapping and lifecycle commands, so that a retried request never creates a duplicate version, mapping or duplicate side effect.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a request is retried with the same tenantId+idempotencyKey and identical payload, When it is reprocessed, Then the original result is returned without re-executing the write, And the same key with a different payload returns a conflict error rather than silently applying the new payload (Idempotency §55).

Summary: Expire idempotency keys per policy
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want idempotency keys to expire after the configured retry/recovery window, so that the idempotency_records collection does not grow unbounded and stale keys don't block legitimate re-use.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an idempotency record has passed its expiresAt timestamp, When a cleanup/TTL process runs, Then the record is purged and the key becomes available for reuse (Idempotency §55).

Summary: Use MongoDB transactions for coupled curriculum writes
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want curriculum, version, history and outbox writes that must succeed or fail together to be wrapped in a MongoDB transaction, so that partial writes never leave the system in an inconsistent state.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum create or publish operation touches curricula, curriculum_versions, curriculum_history and outbox_events, When the operation executes, Then all writes commit atomically or none do, and downstream consistency is achieved eventually via published events (Transaction Strategy §56).

Summary: Security, RBAC & Audit Governance
Description: Enforce the full curriculum permission set across all actor roles (including the diagram's Accreditation Team and External API), classify data sensitivity, and maintain an immutable audit trail. Satisfies FR-12, FR-13, §47–50.

Summary: Enforce granular RBAC permissions on every curriculum action
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want every endpoint to check a granular permission code (CURRICULUM_VIEW/CREATE/EDIT/SUBMIT/REVIEW/APPROVE/PUBLISH/RETIRE, SUBJECT_MAPPING_MANAGE, SYLLABUS_MANAGE, OUTCOME_MAPPING_MANAGE, PREREQUISITE_MANAGE, CURRICULUM_EXPORT), so that only authorized actors can perform each action.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a user attempts an action without the corresponding permission code for their role, When the request reaches the service, Then it is rejected with ACD2_FORBIDDEN (403) before any business logic executes, and the full permission matrix in §48 is enforced consistently across every endpoint.

Summary: Scope Department Head permissions to their own department's curricula
Description: As a Department Head, I want my curriculum view/edit/approve permissions limited to curricula owned by my department, so that I cannot act on curricula outside my authority.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am a Department Head for a specific department, When I attempt to view, edit or approve a curriculum whose departmentId differs from mine, Then the action is denied with ACD2_FORBIDDEN (403) regardless of my role-level permissions (RBAC §48, Actors and Personas §8).

Summary: Grant the Accreditation Team read-only access for compliance and audit
Description: As an Accreditation Team member, I want read-only access to curriculum structure, outcomes and history through the Accreditation Portal, so that I can verify compliance and audit trails without any ability to modify curriculum data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as Accreditation Team, When I access curriculum, outcome or history data via the Accreditation Portal, Then I receive read-only results scoped to compliance/audit views, consistent with 'View for compliance and audit' (RBAC panel 8 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Grant External API consumers scoped read-only access
Description: As an External API consumer, I want read-only access limited to the scope defined for my API key, so that I can consume published curriculum data without any write capability or over-broad visibility.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call any ACD-02 endpoint, Then I receive only the data within my granted scope and read-only access, matching 'Read-only access (as per scope)' (RBAC panel 8 of the architecture diagram).

Summary: Record an immutable, append-only history entry for every material change
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want every version creation, mapping, submission, approval, publication and retirement to be recorded as an append-only entry in curriculum_history, so that a complete, tamper-evident audit trail always exists.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any material mutation occurs (create, version, mapping, submit, approve, publish, retire), When the mutation commits, Then a corresponding curriculum_history record is written capturing action, actorId, timestamp and before/after context, and history records can never be updated or deleted (Audit Model §46).

Summary: Classify and protect curriculum data by sensitivity level
Description: As a Security Architect, I want curriculum data classified into L1 Public, L2 Internal, L3 Confidential and L4 Highly Restricted tiers, so that access controls and exposure match each field's sensitivity.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a field is classified L3 (approval/history/actor metadata) or L4 (security/configuration data), When a user without sufficient clearance queries curriculum data, Then those fields are excluded from the response while L1 public catalog summaries remain visible per role (Data Classification §49).

Summary: Encrypt curriculum data at rest and in transit
Description: As a Security Architect, I want all ACD-02 service communication encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and MongoDB data encrypted at rest, so that curriculum data is protected against interception and storage compromise.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-02 is deployed to any environment, When traffic flows between clients, the API gateway and MongoDB, Then TLS 1.2+ is enforced end-to-end, encryption at rest is enabled, backups are encrypted, and sensitive audit fields are masked in logs (Encryption and Secrets §50).

Summary: Observability, Reliability & Performance
Description: Provide structured logging, metrics, tracing, alerting and defined SLOs so operations can detect, diagnose and recover from failures quickly. Satisfies §51–54, §57–59.

Summary: Emit structured logs with correlation context
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want every ACD-02 request to emit a structured log with timestamp, service, tenantId, requestId, correlationId, actorId, operation and outcome, so that I can trace any request end-to-end across services.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any API call to ACD-02, When the request completes (success or failure), Then a structured log entry containing all required fields is emitted, and correlationId propagates through to any published events (Logging and Observability §51).

Summary: Expose operational metrics and distributed tracing
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want request rate, latency, error rate, DB latency, event rate, publication rate and validation-failure rate exposed as metrics, plus end-to-end tracing from Gateway through ACD-02 to ACD-01/03, MongoDB/outbox, broker and consumers, so that I can monitor service health and diagnose issues.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-02 is running in production, When metrics are scraped and traces are sampled, Then all listed metrics are available on the monitoring dashboard and a trace can be followed across the full request path (§51).

Summary: Alert on SLO-breaching and reliability signals
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want alerts configured for 5xx spikes, P95/P99 latency breach, MongoDB health/replication issues, outbox backlog age, event publication failures, DLQ growth, approval-workflow failures, reference-service latency, index/query degradation, storage growth and unauthorized-access spikes, so incidents are caught before they impact users.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any monitored signal crosses its defined threshold, When the breach is sustained beyond the alerting window, Then an alert fires to the on-call channel with enough context to begin triage (Monitoring and Alerting §52).

Summary: Apply bounded retry with exponential backoff for transient failures
Description: As the Curriculum Management Service, I want transient failures (broker unavailable, MongoDB timeout, reference-service latency) to be retried with exponential backoff and jitter up to a bounded limit, so that temporary issues self-heal without manual intervention or infinite retry storms.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a transient failure occurs on a retryable operation, When the retry policy executes, Then attempts back off exponentially with jitter up to a maximum bound, and validation/authorization errors are never retried (Retry Strategy §54).

Summary: Meet indexed read/write performance targets
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want curriculum reads, search, version create/update and mapping writes to meet their defined P95 latency targets via proper indexing, so that the service remains responsive at institutional scale.
Acceptance Criteria: Given production-representative load, When each workload type is exercised, Then normal API latency P95 <300ms and curriculum reads P95 <500ms are met using indexed access paths, verified in performance testing (NFR §16, Performance §59).

Summary: Validate disaster recovery via regular restore tests
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want automated MongoDB backups with tested restore procedures, so that ACD-02 can meet its defined RPO/RTO in a disaster scenario.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the configured backup schedule, When a scheduled restore test is executed against a non-production environment, Then the restored dataset is verified complete and consistent (Disaster Recovery and Backup §57).

Summary: Scale application tier and event throughput horizontally
Description: As a Platform Architect, I want ACD-02's application tier and event throughput to scale horizontally under load while maintaining zero direct database sharing with other services, so the service can absorb institutional growth without redesign.
Acceptance Criteria: Given increased request or event volume, When autoscaling policies trigger, Then additional capacity is provisioned without service interruption, and multi-tenancy/zero-DB-sharing invariants are preserved (Scalability §58, NFR §16).

Summary: API Standards, Error Handling & Contracts
Description: Deliver a consistent, versioned REST contract with standardized request/response envelopes and the full documented error taxonomy across all ACD-02 endpoints. Cross-cutting.

Summary: Publish and version the ACD-02 API contract
Description: As an API Consumer, I want a versioned specification covering every /api/v1/academics/curricula endpoint (create, search, detail, versions, semesters, subjects, syllabus, outcomes, prerequisites, submit, approve, publish, retire, history), so that I can integrate against a stable, documented contract.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-02 service, When the API contract is published, Then it documents every endpoint in the REST API Specification (§28) with request/response schemas, and breaking changes require a new API version.

Summary: Return standardized success and error envelopes
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every response to follow the standard {success, data, meta} / {success:false, error, meta} envelope with requestId and correlationId, so that clients can handle responses uniformly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any ACD-02 API call, When the response is returned, Then it conforms to the Standard Response / Error Response shapes in §29.3/29.4.

Summary: Map every domain exception to a documented error code and HTTP status
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every failure condition (curriculum not found, invalid course/subject reference, immutable version, version conflict, publication blocked, duplicate mapping, credit policy violation, prerequisite cycle, forbidden, dependency unavailable) mapped to a specific error code and HTTP status, so that I can build reliable client-side error handling.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each documented failure condition occurs, When the API responds, Then it returns the exact code/HTTP pairing defined in Error Handling §53 (e.g. ACD2_CURRICULUM_NOT_FOUND/404, ACD2_COURSE_INVALID/422, ACD2_SUBJECT_INVALID/422, ACD2_VERSION_IMMUTABLE/409, ACD2_VERSION_CONFLICT/409, ACD2_PUBLICATION_BLOCKED/409, ACD2_DUPLICATE_MAPPING/409, ACD2_CREDIT_POLICY/422, ACD2_PREREQUISITE_CYCLE/422, ACD2_FORBIDDEN/403, ACD2_DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE/503).

Summary: End-to-End Scenarios & Cross-Module Integration
Description: Validate complete cross-cutting flows spanning creation, mapping, approval, publication and every listed downstream module integration (ACD-01, ACD-03, ACD-04, EXM, STM, HRM, COM, ACD-10). Satisfies Testing Strategy §67 and Cross-Module Integration panel 10.

Summary: E2E: Create → Map Subjects → Submit → Approve → Publish
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test that creates a curriculum, maps subjects to semesters, submits it for approval, approves and publishes it, and verifies downstream services receive the CurriculumPublished event, so that the full authoritative-curriculum lifecycle is proven to work together.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a fresh curriculum is created via UC-01, When it is versioned, mapped, submitted, approved and published per Workflow §14.1, Then ACD-01, ACD-03, EXM, LMS and Analytics local projections reflect the published curriculum via consumed events, verified end-to-end (Testing Strategy §67).

Summary: E2E: Annual revision preserves prior version and history
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test proving that an annual revision clones the effective version into a draft, applies changes, and publishes a new effective version while the prior version is retained and superseded, so that BR-11/BR-12 are continuously verified.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum has a currently effective version, When Workflow §14.2 (Annual Revision) is executed end-to-end, Then the new version becomes effective, the prior version is marked SUPERSEDED and remains queryable, and CurriculumVersionCreated/CurriculumPublished events are observed by consumers.

Summary: E2E: publication blocked when a mapped subject is deactivated
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test that deactivates a subject mapped into a pending curriculum version and verifies publication is blocked, so that the SubjectDeactivated event-consumption rule is continuously verified against a realistic scenario.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a curriculum version has a subject mapping for subjectId=SUB-101, When ACD-03 emits SubjectDeactivated for SUB-101 and a publish is then attempted, Then the mapping is flagged and publication is rejected with ACD2_SUBJECT_INVALID/ACD2_PUBLICATION_BLOCKED, verified end-to-end (Event Consumption §32).

Summary: Validate integrations with ACD-01, ACD-03, ACD-04, EXM, STM, HRM, COM and ACD-10 before production sign-off
Description: As a Release Manager, I want end-to-end integration tests against every module listed in the Cross-Module Integration table executed as part of the Production Definition of Done, so that ACD-02 is not released until its downstream contracts are proven.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-02 release candidate, When the full integration test suite runs against ACD-01 (course details), ACD-03 (subject details), ACD-04 (batch validation), EXM (scheme/assessment mapping), STM (enrollment curriculum), HRM (faculty subject mapping), COM (curriculum-change notifications) and ACD-10 (curriculum analytics), Then all contract, event-schema and E2E scenarios pass, and this gate is required before the service is marked production-ready (Production Definition of Done §68, Cross-Module Integration panel 10).
